history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration design a common set of performance measures to improve consistency of reporting to Member States.
history.administration_response: Closure of this recommendation is requested, as it has been overtaken by events. The recommendation was made in 2015, and the subsequent United Nations management reform separated strategy, policy and guidance from operational management and further extended the delegation of authority to individual entities. Following this reform, the Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance, the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget, the Field Operations Finance Division and the Global Asset Management Policy Service are responsible for providing policy and guidance, while responsibility for operational management lies within each individual entity, which is responsible for defining and managing its own performance. The requested common set of performance measures relates to recording and reporting on the “quality and timeliness of facilities services”, and it is derived from specific service cases in individual entities. It is therefore not within the scope of policy and guidance oversight, but falls within the micromanagement tasks of each entity. In addition, there is no common tool or system that would bring together records or requested statistics for the whole United Nations system, so coordination of reporting and data collection would require additional resources.
history.board_assessment: Given that the requested common set of performance measures relates to recording and reporting on the “quality and timeliness of facilities services”, and that it is derived from specific service cases in individual entities after management reform, the Board considers this recommendation as having been overtaken by events.
